requirements.name: geometry
requirements.check: Decode assets/working.png as exactly 64x16: four horizontal 16x16 cells at x=0,16,32,48 with no gutters or added canvas between or around the cells (transparent margin inside a cell is composition, not padding). Consumer basis (unchanged original module src/queue-view.ts lines 4 and 9; identical constants in the proposed successor module lines 8 and 13): running frames 4 (the sheet's cell count, unchanged under either preference), display.cell [16,16] and frameMs 100. Fixture behaviour, descriptive only and scoped to this successor destination as designed: the successor fixture draws only when width == 16*frames and height == 16, slices frame*16,0,16,16 and derives the frame from frameAt() (floor(elapsed/100) mod 4 when animating; the held cell otherwise).
requirements.reason: Fresh decode records exact target geometry: Working64x16, Retry/Paused16x16. All actual rendered crops match source dimensions and horizontal cell rectangles.

requirements.name: transparent-exterior-measured
requirements.check: MEASURED record (mechanical/local, diagnostic): retain every cell's alpha histogram and exact RGBA component boxes (zero-based, half-open). FLAG for visual review any alpha>0 component touching all four cell edges, or any single alpha>0 component covering more than half of the cell's 256 pixels. The flag is a diagnostic proxy for a canvas matte or grey tile and is NOT a rejection condition (a corner-to-corner X or full-span glyph legitimately touches all four edges with a transparent exterior). RGB values of alpha-0 pixels are not significant. PROPOSAL (seed-rotation construction only): mechanical REJECTION is decidable only under that construction, where each cell's alpha channel must equal that of cw^k(seed) under dst(x,y)=src(y,15-x) (for the current seed 21f5baca...: measured 224 alpha-0 / 32 alpha-255 pixels per cell). Outside that construction the measured record carries no rejection rule.
requirements.reason: Fresh per-cell alpha histograms, exact RGBA boxes and4-connected components retained. Flags are diagnostic only. Working seed-rotation alpha and visibleRGBA equality pass all4cells under the scoped seed-rotation proposal; selective/full alpha remains permitted.

requirements.name: transparent-exterior-visual
requirements.check: VISUAL record (visual/visual; the deciding rule): viewed at 1x and 3x on #172336, the exterior of every frame, including the held cell when stationary shows the panel with no unintended matte, tile, plate, halo or fringe; a deliberate opaque backing shape is acceptable only when it is part of the mark's recorded design and the exterior stays transparent. Partial alpha on mark pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required. The rejected generated frame whose background held 193 opaque #808080 pixels is the failure class, not the definition of the rule.
requirements.reason: Viewed native and3x colour/gray marks and rendered panel exterior. Negative space remains panel; no unintended solid tile, fringe or halo. Alpha diagnostics were not used as the deciding visual rule.

requirements.name: frame-assembly
requirements.check: For the successor the candidate sheet is the existing assets/working.png (sha256 cf101610...), already the exact 64x16 four-cell sheet, so no assembly step occurs and this clause is satisfied vacuously; the retained record must still name the exact candidate bytes and their provenance (byte-identical to accepted live.working-animation-motion-01.candidate; cells equal cw^k(seed) on alpha and visible RGBA). If a future provider result is not already the exact 64x16 four-cell sheet, the retained assembly record names the exact source frames or cell rectangles in play order and every delivered cell is a lossless copy: identical alpha everywhere and identical RGBA where alpha>0 (RGB of alpha-0 pixels is not significant); no resize, resample or recolor; no undocumented duplication or silent frame drop (a deliberately repeated phase is allowed when the record says so); all raw provider outputs are retained beside the assembled strip.
requirements.reason: No assembly executed: cf101610108f5a708987dfeb1a86ae9921525464d24c19953a889e20603176dc reused byte-identically from live.working-animation-motion-01.candidate. Fresh rotation checks identify cells0..3 as clockwise seed rotations and preserve all cells.

requirements.name: activity-not-success
requirements.check: Viewed at 1x and 3x nearest on #172336 (beside the exact Ready baseline as the comparison method). REQUIRED (owner, BRIEF line 3; PLAR 560-570 state_meaning): the running loop reads as ongoing activity and not as completion, with no completion/success silhouette or success-like terminal pose in the loop. REQUIRED (caller update, PLAR line 422; judged in stationary-meaning): the held cell, shown alone under reduced motion, reads as activity and not as completion. EXPERT CLAUSE (specialist; scope this successor): each transient frame (cells 1-3), seen singly, also reads as activity rather than completion, because frames are exposed singly for 100 ms and frame 0 is painted at cell creation.
requirements.reason: All four exposed poses and chronological observed rotations show separated perimeter clusters. None forms the Ready check or terminal success pose; held frame0 reads a stationary incomplete progress ring.

requirements.name: motion-continuity
requirements.check: Under normal motion, play the actual four frames at the consumer's 100 ms per frame including the fourth-to-first wrap, at 1x and 3x on #172336. Required outcome: the strip plays as one continuous activity loop with no visible discontinuity at the fourth-to-first wrap. All four frames remain in the sheet and in play under normal motion; the reduced-motion hold does not remove or reorder them.
requirements.reason: Inspected actual ordered normal-start and normal-restored exposures, including repeated 3-to-0 wraps at both scales in retained render. Quarter-turn phases preserve one rotating activity motif without a visible end-pose discontinuity. Sampled paint/exposure clocks distinguish actual exposure from synthetic timeline; continuous exact100ms cadence is not claimed.

requirements.name: style-coherence

requirements.reason: Native/3x colour and gray views show compact readable silhouettes, deliberate stepped clusters and related perceptible cool-blue accents against exact Ready. Start remains vector control/color reference. No palette-count,alpha,stroke-width or margin gate imposed.

evidence.declaration_text:
Run one pixel-art command on a drawing or image you already made. This is
the engine's own command line: it checks work, explains it and improves it.

Commands: check and explain (read-only):
- lint <id> [--rules outline_gap,orphan_pixel,…] — pixel-art defects, each
  naming the node and command that drew them
- inspect <id> --region x0,y0,x1,y1 --scale 10 — a zoomed crop with its
  exact colours
- measure <id> --at x,y — what is at a pixel and who drew it
- explain <id> — resolved geometry, per-command footprints, before rendering
- motion / storyboard / silhouette / reveal / clusters / parts <id> — reports
- score <id> — a 0-100 pixel-art discipline score with a breakdown
- compare <id> <id> — two results side by side
Improve (returns a NEW drawing id):
- shade <id> --band 2 --light=-1,-1 — banded shading along a colour ramp
- selout <id> — selective outlining; reoutline / clean-lines / aa / mirror
- cluster <id> --at x,y --action recolor --color <name> — one guarded cluster
- repair <id> — deterministic cleanup of drift, strays, fringe and noise
Sheets and frames (returns a NEW image id):
- split <image> --grid 3x3 — a sprite sheet, strip or grid as an animation,
  one frame per cell (columns x rows)
- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures
  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation
- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a
  4x4 block (a sticker, a print); nothing is redrawn
A result comes back as an image in the reply AND as a no-auth URL the reply
prints, `/mcp/pixel-tools/<id>/image.png` (`frames.png` for the frames of a
multi-frame one) — so a sheet you joined is both readable inline and
downloadable. Sheets hold at most 1024 px a side; `join` refuses a larger
one rather than shrinking the art, and says how many frames do fit.
Craft operations need colour ramps: run `extract-palette <id>` first, then
pass `--ramps skin=dark,mid,light`.
Authoring: `edit <id> --changes '[…]'` applies exact pixel operations and
`draw <id> --recipe '{…}'` builds or revises a layered scene; both take JSON
whose fields are NOT listed here. Colours in that JSON are always `#RRGGBB`
or `#RRGGBBAA` with alpha `00` or `ff` — `rgb()` and bare hex are refused,
and nothing strips the `#`, since argv is a JSON list rather than a shell
line. Every `edit` change carries `operation`, `layer`, `frames` (ONE-based)
and `reason`; coordinates are zero-based and a `region` is `[x0,y0,x1,y1]`
inclusive. Then its own fields: `patch_pixels` takes `pixels`, a list of
`[x,y,expected,replacement]` (1-10000, each assigned only where the pixel
already holds `expected`, so a mismatch fails the pass); `copy_region` takes
`source_layer`, `source_frame`, `region`, `at` `[x,y]`; `map_colors` takes
`region` and `colors` `{"#from":"#to"}` (alpha must match); `flood_fill`
`seed`/`expected`/`color`; `brush` `points` plus `color`; `outline` `mode`
(outside|inside|recolor|erase). The full contracts and any command's flags
are one free call away: `describe edits | paint | outline | draw | animation
| motion | scenes | review`, `<command> -h`, `describe cli`.
Free for subscribers.

PixelLab AI-powered pixel art generation service.

Use of this service is subject to PixelLab's Terms of Service:
https://pixellab.ai/termsofservice

This MCP server provides programmatic access to generate:
- Characters with multiple directional views
- Character animations
- Isometric tiles
- Top-down tilesets for game maps
- Sidescroller tilesets for platformer games

All generation operations are non-blocking and return job IDs for status tracking.
Requires PixelLab subscription (with credit fallback support).

**Pixel tools (free, exact, you are the artist)**: one command line, pixelart_workbench(argv=[...]), inspects, edits, draws and animates pixel art by your own decisions; combine it with the AI tools above. Start with pixelart_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start'], mode='low'|'high') — low acts directly with few tokens, high plans out loud and reviews every frame. Animated effects (spells, hits, explosions, auras): vfx_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start']) — same ids, exports to the user's My effects.

**Git access**: Clone and push game project source code with standard git.
Use `list_projects` to see your projects and their git clone URLs.

declare const tools: { mcp__pixellab__pixelart_workbench(args: {
  // One command line, e.g. 'lint <drawing_id> --rules outline_gap' or ['edit', '<id>', '--changes', '[…]']. Omit it for the playbook. A subject is an id or an image reference — never a file path; the server writes the output and returns a new id. A reference is `character:<id>:<direction>` for a rotation, `character:<id>:<direction>:<animation>` for every frame of that animation (the display name, type or [group: ...] id get_character prints), the same two forms for `object:<id>` (a one-direction object's direction is the literal `unknown`), `gallery:<id>`, `job:<id>`, `upload:<id>`, a data URL, an https link or base64. That is how a stored animation's pixels come back inline without downloading anything. Start with 'describe cli' for the full command list.
  argv?: string | Array<string> | null;
  // low (default): act directly, fewest tokens — one decisive image per result. high: think openly — fuller evidence and a review checklist; write your plan and observations in `notes`. Use the mode the user asked for.
  mode?: "low" | "high";
  // What you observed and what this step should achieve, in a few sentences (high mode: always; low: optional). On the first call, include the user's request. Stored with the step to improve these tools.
  notes?: string | null;
}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
